name: Cleric Debt Collector
body:
Debt collectors specialize in locating offenders, rendering judgment, and collecting payment due. Some debt collectors may work as tax collectors or bounty hunters for nobles or legally sanctioned authorities, while others harbor a vindictive soul and are only interested in settling debts of a personal nature.

A debt collector has the following class features.

Class Skills

A debt collector adds Intimidate, Knowledge (local), and Survival to her list of class skills, and removes Diplomacy.

This alters class skills.

Powerful Personality (Ex)

At 1st level, a debt collector gains Skill Focus (intimidate) as a bonus feat.

Righting a Wrong

All debt collectors have the vengeance inquisition. This alters the cleric’s domains.

Divine Retribution (Sp)

As a standard action, you can point at one creature within 30 feet to indicate that it is the target of divine wrath. A mishap or an accident appropriate to the environment occurs, such as a branch falling on the creature, rocks falling from the ceiling, or some other nonmagical misfortune; regardless of the cause, the mishap deals 1d6 points of damage + 1 point for every two inquisitor levels you possess (Reflex half). The GM decides whether this damage is bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage.

You can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier.

Final Vengeance (Su)

At 8th level, once per day, you can make one melee attack against an opponent within reach in response to an attack that would reduce you to negative hit points. Once your attack is resolved, you suffer the normal effect of the attack that provoked this ability. Effects that kill you or do not reduce you to negative hit points (such as ability damage or drain, negative levels, and disintegrate) do not trigger this ability.

Domain Spells: 1st—command, deadeye’s lore; 2nd—castigate, focused scrutiny; 3rd—burst of speed, righteous vigor; 4th—rebuke, terrible remorse; 5th—mass castigate, litany of vengeance; 6th—eyebite, find the path; 7th—jolting portent, major curse; 8th—discern location, frightful aspect; 9th—storm of vengeance, winds of vengeance. A debt collector must prepare one of these two spells in her domain slot each day.

Reckoning (Su)

At 1st level, once per day as a move action, a debt collector may choose 1 target within sight upon which to issue a reckoning. The reckoning remains in effect for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 the debt collector’s level (minimum 1) + her Charisma modifier. As part of the swift action used to initiate a reckoning, a debt collector can make one Intimidate skill check (DC 10 + the target’s Hit Dice + the target’s Wisdom modifier) with a bonus equal to 1/2 her debt collector level (minimum 1). (The target senses the power of the debt collector, so a common language is not necessary to attempt this check.) If the check is successful, the target is shaken for the duration of the reckoning. A debt collector cannot attempt an Intimidate skill check against a creature lacking an Intelligence score.

A debt collector adds her Charisma modifier as a bonus to a variety of rolls while under the effects of a reckoning.

She adds her Charisma modifier as a bonus to attack rolls against the target of her reckoning, as a deflection bonus to her armor class against attacks from the target of her reckoning, and as a morale bonus to her Will saving throws against any mind affecting effects generated by the target of her reckoning. Finally, at the start of her reckoning, a debt collector gains a number of temporary hit points equal to 1d6. At 3rd level, and every odd level thereafter, the number of temporary hit points gained increases by +1d6.

Any temporary hit points remaining at the end of the debt collector’s reckoning disappear. At 3rd level, and every four levels thereafter, a debt collector can issue a reckoning one additional time per day. For the purposes of the feat Extra Channel only, this ability is treated as the channel energy class feature.

This replaces channel energy.
